elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: Company may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement ... without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: Contractor shall not in any event assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right for Contractor appears in the clause or elsewhere; condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Only "Company may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor"; Contractor has no successor carve-out
No notice mechanic in the redline: "may assign this Agreement without consent"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld

reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are satisfied: Customer affiliate and successor carve-out, Vendor consent subject to a reasonableness standard, an absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor change-of-control termination right (no such right exists anywhere, so the condition is absent).

Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevant because the locked target level (preferred) is met; the two levels are separate bargains.

Minimality fails the official gates: operation 1 expands 14 words to 60 (ratio 4.29) and changes 73.9% of characters. The same result could be achieved by appending a short proviso anchored to the existing sentence rather than restating the consent language.
Trim the redundant "or transfer" and the rhetorical "in any event" in the competitor bar; the operative concept is already covered by "assign" and an unqualified prohibition.
Intent is preserved: the mutual consent standard and the subcontracting restriction remain effective, no term is left undefined, and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.
